title: Green Technology-Based and Innovative Digital Pedagogy for Sustainability Competence and Work Readiness of Prospective Vocational Teachers
content: This study examines the influence of green technology-based pedagogy and innovative digital-based pedagogy on sustainability competence and work readiness among pro-spective vocational automotive teachers using the SEM-PLS approach. The findings in-dicate that all constructs are valid and reliable, with strong explanatory power (R²  > 0.60), high predictive relevance (Q² = 0.858), and good model fit (GoF = 0.647). Both pedagog-ical approaches significantly and positively affect sustainability competence, with in-novative digital-based pedagogy having the strongest impact. Furthermore, sustaina-bility competence strongly influences work readiness and fully mediates the relationship between the two pedagogical approaches and work readiness. This suggests that en-hancing sustainability competence is essential in preparing future vocational teachers for the workforce. The study also extends the TPACK framework by integrating sus-tainability into the Green-TPACK model. Practically, the results emphasize the need to strengthen green and digital pedagogies through the integration of green skills, digital technology utilization, and contextual learning to improve sustainability competence and support work readiness in the era of sustainable industry.
